claims.text: A Deployment declares replicas, a selector and a Pod template; the Deployment controller creates a ReplicaSet from it, and the ReplicaSet creates the Pods. You do not manage that ReplicaSet directly.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Workloads > Deployments (Creating a Deployment; 'Do not manage ReplicaSets owned by a Deployment')

claims.text: The ReplicaSet created by a Deployment is named [DEPLOYMENT-NAME]-[HASH], the hash being the pod-template-hash of the Pod template; its Pods are named after the ReplicaSet plus a random suffix.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (ReplicaSet name format; Pod-template-hash label)

claims.text: Changing only replicas of a Deployment scales the existing ReplicaSet; no new ReplicaSet is created and running Pods are not replaced (a rollout is triggered only by changes to .spec.template).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (Updating a Deployment: rollout only if template changed; Scaling a Deployment); outputs deployment.txt

claims.text: A Pod deleted from a Deployment is replaced by its ReplicaSet; deleting the Deployment deletes its ReplicaSet and Pods (garbage collection via owner references, cascading delete by default).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Garbage Collection (Owners and dependents; cascading deletion); outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/deployment.txt

claims.text: An owner is the object responsible for another (ownerReferences), usually the one that created it: the Deployment owns its ReplicaSet and the ReplicaSet owns its Pods.
kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/web waits until the Deployment's Available condition is True, i.e. it has at least the minimum number of available Pods.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (Deployment status / Complete Deployment; type: Available); kubectl wait reference

claims.text: kubectl get deployment shows READY (ready/desired), UP-TO-DATE and AVAILABLE; UP-TO-DATE counts replicas updated to the current template.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (Creating a Deployment: fields displayed)

claims.text: Overlapping selectors between a Deployment and another controller such as a ReplicaSet are not prevented by Kubernetes and the controllers may conflict and behave unexpectedly.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (Selector: do not overlap labels or selectors with other controllers)

claims.text: deploy/k8s/lessons/web-deployment.yaml@stage-2: Deployment web in donhang, replicas 3, selector app: web, template app: web, caddy:2.10.0; differs from web-replicaset.yaml only in kind (and comments).
At stage-2, deploy/k8s/api.yaml, db.yaml, redis.yaml, keycloak.yaml, mailpit.yaml declare kind: Deployment; the only ReplicaSet manifest in the repository is deploy/k8s/lessons/web-replicaset.yaml.

scripts/k8s/deployment.sh@stage-2 lines 14-35 apply web-deployment.yaml, wait Available, list deployment/replicaset/pods, scale to 5 via sed, show one ReplicaSet at 5 and 3 of 3 earlier Pods, delete the Deployment, then nothing with app=web remains.
caddy:2.10.0 is the Caddy web server image that docker-compose.yml@stage-2 runs as service web.
